doc.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: Collective Black Artists' Orchestra
summary: Jimmy Owens was behind the orchestra, which gave Hampton freedom to experiment.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Oh gosh. I didn’t ask you about the Black Artists’ Orchestra, the Manhattan Composers’ Orchestra.

Oh yeah. That orchestra I think Jimmy Owens had a great deal to do with that orchestra. And I got to write quite a few things for them. It was a wonderful experience because I was free to do whatever I wanted to, usually some kind of direction in the program, but it was a chance to have the freedom as far as the things that I wanted to try, the things that I wanted to experiment with and all of that. It was a wonderful opportunity for me so I think I had a chance to do a lot of good things there, to learn a lot was one of the main things. And the guys were very willing to try all kinds of things. © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-
